chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa from al-Hasan ibn Mahbub from Abu Ayyub from Sama'ah ibn Mihran said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a man who married an Umm al-Walad (concubine who bore a child) who belonged to a man, and her master died, and the deceased had a child from someone other than his Umm al-Walad. Do you see if the one who married the Umm al-Walad wants to marry the daughter of her master (the deceased) whom he freed, is there any harm? He said, 'There is no harm with that.'

key_terms.أُمَّ وَلَدٍ: Concubine who bore a child to her master

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible for a man to marry the daughter of his freed concubine?
ai.summary: This narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the marital eligibility between a man and the daughter of his former *Umm al-Walad* (concubine who bore his master's child) after the master's death. Imam al-Sadiq (AS) permits this union, distinguishing it from prohibitions involving direct lineage or nursing kinship, thereby highlighting the flexibility in Shia jurisprudence regarding freed slaves' families. The ruling underscores that the bond of *Umm al-Walad* does not create an impediment to marriage with her offspring, provided the child is not from the same mother.
